message.content:
Map the existing email/mailbox infrastructure in the Nxeon codebase at /opt/nxeon so I can build an ADMIN-portal feature that creates FREE mailboxes on the company domain nxeon.cloud (admin@, support@, santino@, plus create-more), and read their inbox. Be thorough and return concrete file paths, function signatures, model fields, and env var names — not prose. Cover:

1. MAILCOW API CLIENT: Find the module that talks to Mailcow (likely lib/mailcow*.ts or similar). List every exported function with its signature — especially: create a mailbox, delete a mailbox, list mailboxes, set/reset a mailbox password, create aliases, check/add a domain. What env vars configure it (Mailcow base URL, API key)? What's the exact HTTP shape (endpoints like /api/v1/add/mailbox)? Include how errors are handled.

2. CUSTOMER MAILBOX PROVISIONING TODAY: How are customer mailboxes created now? Find the Prisma model(s) (EmailSubscription? Mailbox?) with ALL their fields, the server action(s) that create a mailbox (lib/actions-mail.ts or similar), how the domain is chosen, how the mailbox password/credentials are stored (encrypted? plaintext? a column name), and how billing/subscription is attached (so I know how to make an admin mailbox FREE / bypass billing).

3. WEBMAIL / IMAP READER: How does /dashboard/mail read an inbox? Find the IMAP client code, the API routes (app/api/mail/*), and the actions (listFolders, list messages, read message, send). How does it authenticate to IMAP for a given mailbox (where do the creds come from)? Is nxeon.cloud already configured as a Mailcow domain, and where is the mail host/IMAP host configured?

4. ADMIN PORTAL CONVENTIONS: How is an admin page structured (look at 2-3 examples under app/admin/*/page.tsx)? Where is the admin sidebar nav defined (the list of admin nav items + icons)? How does admin RBAC work — the requireArea / admin-group / rbac helper used at the top of admin pages and admin server actions (lib/rbac.ts, lib/admin-groups.ts)? Show the exact guard call pattern an admin page/action uses.

5. Any existing admin-side mail/email management page already present (grep app/admin for mail/email), and the SMTP/mail settings surface.

Return a structured reference I can build directly from.

5	/**
6	 * Role-based access control for the admin ops portal.
7	 *
8	 * The admin surface is divided into logical *areas*. Each area maps to the set
9	 * of staff roles allowed to see and use it. ADMIN implicitly has every area.
10	 * The admin layout uses this to (a) let any staff role in and (b) hide nav
11	 * items a role can't reach; each sensitive page additionally gates itself with
12	 * `requireArea(...)` so a hand-typed URL is refused too.
13	 */
14	export type Area =
15	  | "overview"
16	  | "analytics"
17	  | "clients"
18	  | "support"
19	  | "fleet"
20	  | "billing"
21	  | "platform";
22	
23	/** Which roles may access each area. ADMIN is always allowed (see canAccess). */
24	export const AREA_ROLES: Record<Area, Role[]> = {
25	  overview: ["SUPPORT", "BILLING", "ADMIN"],
26	  analytics: ["ADMIN"],
27	  clients: ["SUPPORT", "ADMIN"],
28	  support: ["SUPPORT", "ADMIN"],
29	  fleet: ["ADMIN"],
30	  billing: ["BILLING", "ADMIN"],
31	  platform: ["ADMIN"],
32	};
33	
34	export function canAccess(role: Role, area: Area): boolean {
35	  return role === "ADMIN" || AREA_ROLES[area].includes(role);
36	}
37	
38	/** Any non-customer role that belongs in the ops portal. */
39	export function isStaff(role: Role): boolean {
40	  return role === "SUPPORT" || role === "BILLING" || role === "ADMIN";
41	}
42	
43	/** Maps admin nav hrefs to their governing area. Unknown routes default to platform (ADMIN-only). */
44	const HREF_AREA: Record<string, Area> = {

88	  return HREF_AREA[href] ?? "platform";

92	  return canAccess(role, areaForHref(href));

95	/**
96	 * Server-side page guard. Redirects to /login if signed out, or back to the
97	 * overview if the (staff) user's role can't reach this area. Returns the real
98	 * signed-in user (impersonation is refused elsewhere in the admin layout).
99	 */
100	export async function requireArea(area: Area): Promise<User> {
101	  const user = await realUser();
102	  if (!user) redirect("/login");
103	  if (!isStaff(user.role)) redirect("/dashboard");
104	  if (!canAccess(user.role, area)) redirect("/admin");
105	  return user;
106	}
